subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should OpenClaw permanently treat ClawHub, bundled metadata, and official-catalog mappings as trusted for the new provenance gate while requiring --force for arbitrary sources and refusing those sources in Crestodian?
rationale: Tests can prove the implementation, but they cannot choose the intended trust taxonomy or whether expanding the public --force contract is an acceptable upgrade change.

options.title: Approve the documented boundary
options.body: Accept the centralized trust classifier, expanded --force acknowledgement semantics, and Crestodian trusted-only rule after a fresh rebase review.

options.title: Use a dedicated acknowledgement flag
options.body: Keep the source warning but preserve --force as overwrite-only and retain the existing --link incompatibility contract.

options.title: Pause the policy change
options.body: Keep current install behavior until maintainers define a broader plugin provenance and ClawHub trust policy.

recommendation.title: Approve the documented boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the centralized trust classifier, expanded --force acknowledgement semantics, and Crestodian trusted-only rule after a fresh rebase review.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin install, persistence, and security review history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the permanent trust-boundary decision.
